subject: Future Tech
title: Quantum Error Correction
description: A quick, practical guide to Quantum Error Correction.

hook.text: Qubits make errors constantly. Without correction, a long quantum computation would produce meaningless noise.

buildup.text: Classical error correction copies bits. But the no-cloning theorem forbids copying a qubit's quantum state.

discovery.text: Shor and Steane found a workaround: spread one logical qubit across many physical qubits to detect errors.

twist.text: The cost is steep. Protecting one logical qubit may require a thousand physical ones. Scale just got harder.

climax.text: Google's Willow chip showed error rates dropping as more qubits were added, proving the approach can work.

punchline.text: Quantum computing's future rests on taming its errors.

quiz.question: Why can't quantum error correction simply copy a qubit?
